propositions: Plans assert that named modules provide or lack capabilities, but these assertions are false against the actual code (capability-surface mismatch)
The existing E4 probe misses capability-surface defects because it only checks module existence, not the finer-grained capability presence/absence
A new advisory, code-grounded, agent-tier criterion 'asserted-capability' must be registered in the G6/E4 rubric family with posture advisory and facet codebase-grounding

The criterion uses the existing four-pass finder/verifier/decide/coach machinery to check both directions: plan claims module provides capability but it lacks it, or plan claims capability absent but module provides it

The criterion must be registered with routing, rubric prompt, and guide documentation, and must pass deterministic unit tests and bounded sanity checks on the three E1-verified misses (dc58, db7b, 5886)
Promotion from advisory to blocking is future dogfood-gated and auto-recorded by the standing criterion_effectiveness.py recorder with zero per-criterion wiring
